plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.

conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier returns around 1.5% per month. The focus is on capital preservation, significantly reducing leverage and concentration risk. Expect lower drawdowns but also capped upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%) to reduce risk.
Trim SPY to 25% to address concentration.
Increase SMH to 17% to add semiconductor exposure.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% monthly growth by blending broad market exposure with quality tech and limited leverage. It aims for risk-first growth, keeping drawdowns manageable while seeking reasonable upside. Leverage is kept low.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and free up capital.
Increase leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 6% each.
Boost SMH to 19% and CRWD to 15% to concentrate on strong tech.
Reduce QQQI to 10% to shift focus from income to growth.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by increasing leverage and concentration in high-scoring names.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly growth by leaning into leverage and concentrated high-conviction tech/semiconductor names. Expect significantly higher potential upside but also substantially larger drawdowns and the risks associated with leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build a cash buffer.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
Add QQQ to 20% for broad market exposure.
Sell CRWD and SMH entirely to cut high-beta and sector risk.
income.read: This income-focused plan aims for steady monthly distributions around 1% by prioritizing income-generating assets and broad market exposure. It significantly reduces leverage and single-stock risk for lower drawdowns. Distributions are variable and NAV can still decline.
